Washington, DC:US President Donald Trump on Tuesday (local time) claimed that more than 24,000 noncitizens voted illegally in the 2020 election, citing an ongoing review by the US Census Bureau. In a post on Truth Social, Trump said, "The Census Bureau has begun checking the Voter Records from 2020 against their Citizenship Records. On the first 128,000,000 Voters, the Census Bureau proves that over 24,000 Noncitizens voted illegally!" "The Census Bureau is going to analyse the next 32,000,000 Voters, and this number will explode," he added. Trump also reiterated his claim about the 2020 election, saying, “I won the election!” He further called for the passage of the SAVE America Act, saying, "We must pass THE SAVE America Act. Thank you for your attention to this matter!" His remarks came after he endorsed the proposed Safeguard American Voter Eligibility (SAVE) America Act, introduced in Congress on January 29, which aims to overhaul federal voting standards in the United States. It mandates that state election authorities require physical proof of US citizenship (such as a passport or birth certificate) upon voter registration, alongside valid photo identification at the ballot box; limits mail voting strictly to specific exceptions, including illness, physical disability, active military service, or travel; and directs US states to purge non-citizens from federal voter registries using federal databases. "Earlier this month, India's Chief Election Commissioner, Gyanesh Kumar, asked our Administration -- How can you have Elections in the US without a valid Photo ID?" Trump said. Referring to India's last general election, Trump said, "India's last Election had 646,000,000 Voters! headlines.full_text: Ex-prosecutor charged with treason in Mexico over US drug raid César Jáuregui Moreno is accused of allowing US agents to join a raid on a suspected drugs lab in April. Federal prosecutors in Mexico have charged a former state prosecutor with treason for allowing US agents to join a raid on a suspected drugs lab in April without proper authorisation. César Jáuregui Moreno served as attorney general of the northern border state of Chihuahua from 2023 to this year. The involvement of Americans came to light after two US agents said to have worked for the CIA died in a car crash in Chihuahua along with two Mexican law enforcement officers. Attorney General Ernestina Godoy Ramos said Jáuregui had allowed foreign agents to carry out activities reserved for Mexican authorities and had failed to share information. Jáuregui has denied the allegations. The former prosecutor, who is a member of the conservative opposition PAN party, was arrested at the weekend. A court hearing is scheduled for Saturday. A judge must still determine whether there is enough evidence to proceed with the case, Reuters news agency reports. Jáuregui also faces state-level charges in Chihuahua, including of abuse of public office. In a court hearing for those charges on Sunday, he denied that he instructed or consented to the involvement of US agents in the operation. headlines.full_text: Sudan army drones hit mourners and fuel market killing more than 300 people, sources say A truck carrying people to a funeral and a market alleged to be supplying fuel to the RSF were targeted. Sudan's army has been accused of launching several drone strikes that have reportedly killed more than 300 people, including dozens travelling to a funeral. The death toll from strikes in two areas of West Kordofan state on Sunday evening was 150, sources told the Sudan War Observatory, which tracks the conflict that erupted in 2023 between the army and the paramilitary Rapid Support Forces (RSF). In Abyei, a disputed border area between Sudan and South Sudan, 153 people were killed when drones hit a market on Monday, the region's information minister said. A military source told the BBC the army had carried out the Abyei attack, saying the market was a fuel supply site for the RSF. The attack has raised tensions between South Sudan and Sudan, which jointly administer Abyei, as they both claim ownership to the oil-rich region in a dispute that has remained unresolved since South Sudan ceded in 2011. South Sudan has summoned Sudan's ambassador to lodge a formal protest. There are fears the conflict could spill across the border. headlines.full_text: Sudan drone strike kills around 150 in Abyei market A drone strike hit a market in the Abyei border region disputed by Sudan and South Sudan and killed dozens. The drone caused a large fire when it hit a fuel depot. South Sudanese officials blamed Sudan's military. Adrone strikein a busy market in the disputed region of Abyei has killed more than 150 people, according to local officials. South Sudanese officials blamedSudan's military for the attack, without providing evidence, amidthe long-running civil warbetween the Sudanese Armed Forces and the Rapid Support Forces (RSF) militia, which is reportedly active in the Abyei area. The special UN mission in Abyei warned in May that the RSF's presence in the resource-rich region had put residents in additional danger, and risked intensifying the older territorial dispute between Sudan and the world's newest sovereign state,South Sudan. According to local authorities, the attack hit the busy Amiet Market at around midday on Monday. Yohana Akol Ngor, the caretaker information minister in Abyei, told Reuters news agency on Tuesday that the death toll had more than doubled, reaching at least 153 compared to a stated figure of 73 the previous day. He said that Sudan's military was responsible for the attack but did not provide evidence. Akol Ngor said around 8,000 people had been displaced by the bombing. South Sudan's Foreign Ministry also blamed the Sudanese army and said the drone struck multiple locations around the busy market. headlines.full_text: Co-op MOU signed between Chambers of Commerce of Mashhad, Dushanbe TEHRAN- During the trip of the Governor of Khorasan Razavi Province and his accompanying delegation to Tajikistan, a cooperation memorandum was signed between the Chambers of Commerce of Mashhad and Dushanbe with the aim of developing trade interactions and facilitating the activities of traders and businessmen of the two countries. TEHRAN- During the trip of the Governor of Khorasan Razavi Province and his accompanying delegation to Tajikistan, a cooperation memorandum was signed between the Chambers of Commerce of Mashhad and Dushanbe with the aim of developing trade interactions and facilitating the activities of traders and businessmen of the two countries. At the signing meeting, held at the Dushanbe Chamber of Commerce, the issue of Iranian and Tajik traders using the domestic forex rates of the two countries to attend exhibitions and develop exhibition cooperation was discussed and agreed upon. Also, the ground for the presence of Tajik businessmen in the Mashhad Mining Exhibition, which is held in the next Iranian month, was reviewed, and emphasis was placed on providing the possibility of attendance and allocating booths to Tajik traders. Acceptance of Iran’s national standards for goods imported into Tajikistan was another topic raised at this meeting, and it was decided that the necessary follow-ups in this regard would be carried out through the Dushanbe Chamber of Commerce. It is worth noting that at the end of this meeting, the head of the Dushanbe Chamber of Commerce and Tajik economic actors were invited to travel to Khorasan Razavi Province in the coming months at the invitation of the Mashhad Chamber of Commerce, so that the ground for expanding trade and economic cooperation between the two sides would be provided more than before. Aleksandar Vucic, who resigned as Serbia’s president on September 27, has pledged that he will do his utmost not to allow the country to become part of the European Union’s plans to prepare for an armed conflict with Russia. Serbia "is becoming a thorn in the side of Europe as it prepares for a future war with Russia," he told the Prva television channel. "I don’t want Serbia to be part of this war, and I will not let Serbia become part of it." Snap parliamentary elections in Serbia will be held on October 25. Vucic will lead the ruling Serbian Progressive Party’s list and become its candidate for prime minister. His main opponent is 56-year-old cardiologist Ilija Srdanovic from Novi Sad, who leads the Student List coalition.

Chairman of the Alliance of Independent Social Democrats Milorad Dodik told TASS on May 13 that Vladimir Zelensky had attempted to purchase $400 million worth of weapons from Bosnian Muslims. headlines.full_text: Macron accuses foreign leaders of exploiting French riots The comment is an apparent swipe at Benjamin Netanyahu and Donald Trump, who both face elections in coming weeks. French President Emmanuel Macron has accused foreign leaders of exploiting the riots which erupted across the country on Saturday for electoral purposes. Without naming them, he said they were campaigning for forthcoming elections "at France's expense" with their comments on the violence, which erupted on the fringe of cost-of-living protests. Speaking on a visit to the Middle East, he referred to them as "leaders who are in campaign mode, whether here in the region or on the other side of the Atlantic". It was an apparent swipe at Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, who faces parliamentary elections next week, and US President Donald Trump, for whom mid-term polls fall next month. Macron said the unnamed leaders had been influenced by fake videos generated by AI about the riots. Nearly 150 people have been jailed and more than 800 brought before the courts since the riots which gripped Paris and other cities including Lyon, Marseille and Nice. Video of running battles between masked rioters and police, as well as property being destroyed and stores being looted, spread across social media. The government admitted the police had "lost control" during the violence, which came after weeks of protests by students over conditions in high schools. Macron vowed afterwards that the authorities would be "uncompromising" towards "agitators from ultra-left fringe groups", which he blamed for much of the trouble. Clean up begins after French riots but police remain Suspect arrest
headlines.llm_reasoning: Macron accuses unnamed foreign leaders of exploiting the riots for electoral gain, blaming outsiders for domestic unrest.

"Zelensky's not a good guy for us to deal with," Trump told Newsmax last week. The verbal assault has continued this week. headlines.full_text: Katya Adler: France divided over who to blame for riots and what to learn from them In France and beyond there is widespread disagreement over what led to some of the worst unrest seen in French cities in modern history. "This is not the face of France! You media all focus on the violence and destruction of Saturday's protests. But that's not the majority. It's not 'us'. That's not France!" Elisabeth was speaking to me in front of a row of smashed shop windows, shattered glass still littering the tree-lined Parisian street. Its walls were daubed with red-lettered graffiti insulting French police and signed with the date of the riots, 17 October. I'd stopped Elisabeth and her friend to ask their thoughts on what happened on Saturday. Elisabeth was so upset that, when she spoke, she seemed close to tears. "My friend thinks this is civil war in France but I don't. Saturday is about something else entirely." But what did happen exactly? Who was behind the riots? While much of the looting seemed opportunistic, the violence looked pre-planned. Why orchestrate it now, after weeks of student protests? And who most stands to gain from the destruction this weekend? Elisabeth wasn't entirely sure. Different theories are doing the rounds - in and outside France. Black and white answers may be appealing, but the truth is there are many factors at play. The president of the National Assembly, Yaël Braun-Pivet, has proposed a parliamentary inquiry into the riots and how they were organised. French intelligence had briefed government circles earlier this month that left-wing anarchist groups were involved in the student protests. It was the latest in a series ofassaultson Saudi airports as conflict intensifies between Houthi forces and the Saudi-backed internationally recognised Yemeni government. Last week, the kingdom reported that aprojectile strikeon Riyadh’s King Khalid International Airport on October 11 killed one person and injured 11. There are also plans to withdraw family members from a number of other US missions in the region, US officials told Reuters. The United States is interacting with Russia and China on the issue of resolving the US-Israeli military conflict with Iran, US President Donald Trump said. According to Trump, Russia could have participated much more strongly with Iran, and likewise China. "There's relatively little participation. The fact is, both of them would like to see the war settled, so we're in the process of doing that with Russia, and we have China also involved," he told reporters. The United States and Israel launched a war against Iran on February 28. In June, Washington and Tehran signed a memorandum of understanding envisaging an immediate ceasefire on all fronts, including in Lebanon. However, the United States resumed large-scale attacks on Iran overnight to July 8, having accused it of breaching the existing agreements in what concerned the Strait of Hormuz. Later, the US administration actually signaled that it was ceasing the use of military force against Iran and was embarking on a path of its economic suffocation through tougher sanctions.

The vote comes at a time when the province is mourning thedeaths of four soldiers, while dozens of others were injured from a fast-moving fire that burned through a military base in Alberta. While the results of a poll involving 1,021 respondents released byAbacus Dataon Saturday showed that 74% of decided voters favor Alberta remaining within the Canadian Confederation, the independence issue won’t disappear for the nearly 30% who want Alberta’s government to begin the process to hold a binding provincial referendum on whether Alberta should separate from Canada, according to veteran separatist organizer Cory Morgan, who leads a group called Pathway to Independence. Washington:President Donald Trump said Tuesday he was delaying 50% U.S. tariffs on $20 billion worth of Canadian imports after the two countries reached a last-minute deal hours before the sanctions were to go into effect. The announcement, which Trump made on his social media platform, buys time for more negotiations and avoids, for now, another strain in already tense relations between the historic allies. “I have paused the 50% Tariffs against Canada, that were scheduled to kick in tomorrow morning for three days, based on the fact that Canada and the U.S.A., subject to the finalisation of documents, have a DEAL!” Trump posted on Truth Social less than two hours before the 12:01 a.m. Wednesday deadline. If they had gone into effect as scheduled at 12:01 a.m. Wednesday, Trump’s import taxes would have hit Canadian products ranging from hockey sticks to tongue depressors. But the political impact would likely have been bigger than the economic one. Canada had threatened to retaliate against any new tariffs with levies of its own, aggravating a trade fight between countries that sold each other $880 billion worth of goods and services last year. Canadian officials did not immediately respond to requests for comment Tuesday night. Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney and Trump had spoken twice by phone in the past two days about the ongoing negotiations, including a call Tuesday afternoon, Carney’s office said, underscoring the last-minute push for a deal. Wangaratta has been thrust into an unwelcome spotlight this week. Residents in this rural Victorian town are used to catering to tourists passing through on their way to regional wineries, or music lovers visiting its annual jazz and blues festival. Instead, locals are fielding endless questions about their MP - and having to explain to strangers what it all means for the town's nearly 30,000 people. They are clearly in shock about what police say wasa targeted and deliberate attackon Helen Haines on Monday afternoon, when she was struck by a car just outside her office. "People are simply dumbfounded and finding it very hard to fathom the scale of this tragedy," Australia's Governor-General Sam Mostyn, who represents King Charles, said at a press conference on Wednesday. The independent federal MP had to have both legs amputated after she was airlifted to Melbourne. But the "two most important parts of Helen", her heart and her mind, were in "good shape", her husband Phil Haines said. The MP isn't a divisive figure, locals tell the BBC, and no one can understand why she was allegedly targeted. "Everyone knows Helen," says Jane Hill, who owns a giftware shop a few hundred metres down the town's main street from where Haines was hit. "She is a such a good person in our community. She'd go to everything - celebrations, funerals, she's one of those genuinely kind people - and so are her family." CGTN Copied China has strongly condemned Japanese politicians after Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi sent ritual offerings to the war-linked Yasukuni Shrine and some cabinet members and lawmakers visited it. The shrine is a symbol of Japanese militarism and enshrines 14 Class-A war criminals directly responsible for Japan's war of aggression, a spokesperson for the Chinese Embassy in Japan said on Saturday. The 14 were among 28 Japanese Class-A war criminals tried at the International Military Tribunal for the Far East following World War II. Of the 14 enshrined at Yasukuni, seven were sentenced to death by hanging: Hideki Tojo, Kenji Doihara, Iwane Matsui, Heitaro Kimura, Koki Hirota, Seishiro Itagaki and Akira Mutou. The four who were sentenced to life imprisonment: Toshio Shiratori, Kiichiro Hiranuma, Kuniaki Koiso and Yoshijiro Umezu. The one who was sentenced to twenty years in prison: Shigenori Togo. The remaining two enshrined Class-A war criminals: Yusuke Matsuoka and Osami Nagano.

Harvest havoc: on the ground where Zionist settler mobs are running amok Israeli settlers have attacked EU diplomats and an American journalist during the Palestinian olive harvest, RT reports
Read Full Article at RT.com Israeli settlers have attacked Palestinian farmers, European diplomats and an American journalist during the annual olive harvest in the occupied West Bank, as violence against local communities intensifies, RT correspondent Charlotte Dubenskij has reported. The annual olive harvest is a vital source of food and income for Palestinian families, providing both oil for household use and surplus crops to sell. headlines.full_text: The emperor has no clothes: Trump’s parade of power and the naked American empire TEHRAN - In 1837, Danish author Hans Christian Andersen published The Emperor’s New Clothes, the story of a vain ruler deceived into believing he was wearing magnificent garments invisible to fools and those unfit for office. His ministers praised what did not exist, and the public followed, until a child finally cried out: “But he hasn't got anything on!” TEHRAN - In 1837, Danish author Hans Christian Andersen published The Emperor’s New Clothes, the story of a vain ruler deceived into believing he was wearing magnificent garments invisible to fools and those unfit for office. His ministers praised what did not exist, and the public followed, until a child finally cried out: “But he hasn't got anything on!” Nearly two centuries later, Washington appears to be staging its own version of Andersen’s famous procession. Donald Trump continues to parade American power before the world, surrounded by officials applauding his decisions, even as the economic, military and political consequences of his confrontation with Iran expose a far less flattering reality. Andersen’s emperor was not ruined by deception alone, but by the cowardice of those who knew the truth and chose to protect his pride. Washington’s problem today looks remarkably similar. That child’s voice is the only honest sound in West Asia today. It rises from the ruins of Gaza, from the bombed suburbs of Beirut, from the defiant streets of Tehran, screams from the Minab school, from the mountains of Yemen. It says what the courtiers of Washington and Tel Aviv dare not: the American empire is naked. Its clothes are the fiction of victory. Its tailors are the lobbyists and generals who stitch wars from other people’s children. And the emperor, draped in the tattered myth of moral authority, continues his procession while his own people shiver. Look at the latest spectacle.

It now awaits assent, with a minimum two-year wait before going into force. Known as ‘terramation’ or natural organic reduction, a body is placed in a vessel with wood chips, straw, and other plant material. Microbes break down the remains, producing material that can eventually nourish trees and gardens. US operator Recompose says its process takes 8-12 weeks, including a curing period. Remaining bones are mechanically ground down and mixed back in, and artificial implants are removed. Under the NSW bill, families can take the resulting compost home to nourish a memorial tree or garden, or arrange for it to be placed elsewhere. However, choosing to become garden material remains a personal decision; operators are barred from turning a deceased person’s remains into compost against their written wishes. headlines.full_text: Vietnam Airlines Boeing 787 Overruns Munich Runway During Takeoff, Returns Safely A Vietnam Airlines Boeing 787-9 Dreamliner on a Munich-Hanoi flight returned to Munich after a serious incident during takeoff. The aircraft overran the runway, suffered a tailstrike, and experienced tyre damage. Passengers evacuated safely. A Vietnam Airlines Boeing 787-9 Dreamliner operating a Munich-Hanoi flight returned to Munich Airport on Saturday after reportedly suffering a serious incident during takeoff, according to flight-tracking website Flightradar24 and the airline. Flight VN-34, operated by Boeing 787-9 aircraft VN-A867, reportedly rotated extremely late during takeoff and overran the runway before becoming airborne. Preliminary reports said the aircraft travelled around 120 metres beyond the runway end, entering the grass and coming close to the first row of approach lights. The aircraft also reportedly suffered a tailstrike and tyre damage. After takeoff, the aircraft climbed to around 10,000 feet before the crew received a tyre-pressure indication and decided to dump fuel before returning to Munich. Flightradar24 said the aircraft circled for more than two hours to burn fuel. Around 90 minutes after departure, the Boeing 787 made two low approaches to Munich's Runway 26R before landing safely. Smoke was reportedly seen coming from the left main landing gear, after which the aircraft became disabled on the runway. Elon Musk has said he is actively considering merging Tesla and SpaceX, his two biggest companies. "Do I think it would be a good idea? Yes," Musk said during a call with financial analysts to discuss SpaceX's latest results on Tuesday. While Musk noted it could not be assumed a merger will go ahead, and it would need shareholders' support, he said special committees within both companies had been formed to examine the move. "The special committees have not reached agreement on terms of any transaction and there's no guarantee that they will," he said. "But I do think there is a lot of merit to merging and a lot to be gained."
